name: Lebrija

climate: Few classic table-wine grapes keep their freshness in heat like this. It suits fortified wine, table grapes and raisins.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water.
soil.top: The topsoil stores water through dry spells, but stays wet and cold after rain, which slows ripening and can swell the grapes. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Mostly flat. Easy and cheap to farm by machine, but on still nights cold air settles on flat ground, so spring frost is a bigger risk.

winkler: Best for big crops of everyday wine, or table grapes.
